verdicts.title: Boolean Functions with Multiplicative Complexity 3 and 4
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Multiplicative complexity (MC) is defined as the minimum number of AND gates required to implement a function with a circuit over the basis (AND, XOR, NOT). Boolean functions with MC 1 and 2 have been characterized in Fisher and Peralta (2002), and Find et al. (IJICoT 4(4), 222–236, 2017), respectively.
